UPSTREAM: mb/google/sarien: Add psys_pmax setting to 136W This patch adds the setting of psys_pmax to 136W. According to the design, Rpsys is 11.8Kohm. Here is the equation to come out the Psys_pmax value: Psys_pmax * 1.493uA/W * 11.8Kohm / 2 = 1.2V Hence, Psys_pmax is 136W. UPSTREAM: soc/skl: set IGD resources only if device is enabled If the Intel IGD device pci 02.0 is disabled or undefined in the device tree, then internal graphics pre-allocated memory and GFX-VT MMIO memory for virtualization won`t be allocated in the SoC address space. Thus, patch resolves the FSP-S hang problem on Skylake/ Kaby Lake processors when the IGD device is disabled. This should provide to run FSP 2.0-based coreboot on these CPUs families without integrated graphics card. The following boards were used for testing: - Asrock H110M-DVS board (desktop i5-6600) & NVIDIA GTX 1060 as external GPU. Virtualization and GFX 3D acceleration with nouveau driver still works well (tested on VirtualBox 5.1.38 with Ubuntu 18.04.1 as guest and host OS) - Intel KBL-R U RVP board (mobile i5-8350u) without GFX. Payload: tianocore edk2-stable201811-216-g51be9d0. BUG=none BRANCH=none TEST=none Change-Id: I74eb50bacb212621d16b285848d0fc1027722d45 Signed-off-by: Patrick Georgi <pgeorgi@google.com> Original-Commit-Id: 5806665059f1483665c1b2a8ad386e1e90265dcd Original-Change-Id: Id7a0cba582d83e3fe7e8d20342ee219cdd369a53 Original-Signed-off-by: Maxim Polyakov <max.senia.poliak@gmail.com> Original-Reviewed-on: https://review.coreboot.org/c/coreboot/+/32467 Original-Reviewed-by: Nico Huber <nico.h@gmx.de> Original-Tested-by: build bot (Jenkins) <no-reply@coreboot.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1587977 Commit-Ready: Patrick Georgi <pgeorgi@chromium.org> Tested-by: Patrick Georgi <pgeorgi@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Patrick Georgi <pgeorgi@chromium.org>

UPSTREAM: arcada: add internal pull to ISH UART RX We do not want the RX signal to be floating on the board as that could cause the ISH to remain in a higher power state (because there is logic to keep the ISH in an higher power state when there is an active UART). Add an internal 20K pull up on the RX line. In normal configuration this will burn an additional 544uW. FROMGIT: ath10k: add PN replay protection for high latency devices On high latency devices (SDIO, USB) ath10k did not do PN replay check, a data frame with an invalid PN number was not discard as it should have been. So this patch implements PN replay in ath10k. PN replay check for fragmented frames is implemented in followup patch. With low latency devices (PCI, AHB) hardware can store the data frames's content to host memory directly and the firmware can fully reorder data frames, and do PN replay check at the same time. But for high latency devices all data frames will be received and stored in firmware's memory and it is hard to do full reorder because of the memory size limitations in the firmware. This is why the PN replay protections needs to be implemented in host driver. Tested on QCA6174 SDIO with firmware WLAN.RMH.4.4.1-00007-QCARMSWP-1. Signed-off-by: Wen Gong <wgong@codeaurora.org> Signed-off-by: Kalle Valo <kvalo@codeaurora.org> (cherry picked from commit 130c77495708c61f0aa839e436a8a3a973824b19 git://git.kernel.org/pub/scm/linux/kernel/git/kvalo/ath.git ath-next) BUG=b:121980879 TEST=Connect and ping success Change-Id: Ifeee1c9e791f90d889cb0f5115d19f6454bff935 Signed-off-by: Wen Gong <wgong@codeaurora.org> Signed-off-by: Claire Chang <tientzu@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1573222 Reviewed-by: Nicolas Boichat <drinkcat@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Sean Paul <seanpaul@chromium.org>

FROMGIT: ath10k: add fragmentation handler for high latency devices On high latency devices (SDIO, USB) ath10k did not handle fragmented frames and all fragmented frames on receive path were lost in ath10k. Even a simple ping test failed with fragmentation. The fragmented packets are decapsulated based on the security mode, then the PN is checked and the fragmented frame is passed to mac80211. mac80211 in ieee80211_rx_h_defragment() will then combine the fragment frames and forward to upper layers. Tested on QCA6174 SDIO with firmware WLAN.RMH.4.4.1-00007-QCARMSWP-1. platform.MemoryPressure: measure switch times to cold tabs Instead of trying to scale the "initial working set" of tabs to a size that's large enough to induce swapping in systems with large RAM (8 GiB or more), measure tab switch times to the LRU tabs after the first discard. This involves trying to distinguish discarded and crashed tabs. A broken devtools connection means that the tab has either crashed or discarded. After we detect the first discard (via the chrome dbus signal) we assume that a broken connection is due to the discard. This can have false negatives but they should be relatively rare. Before the first discard, broken connections cause fatal errors. Flapjack: Turn off LED when brightness == 0 Currently, when the brightness passed to led_set_brightness is zero, the current is set to 4mA and the pwm duty is set to the brightness. Since duty == 0 means 1/32 (instead of 0/32), this doesn't turn off the LED. This patch makes the current explicitly set to 0mA if the brightness is zero. Signed-off-by: Daisuke Nojiri <dnojiri@chromium.org> BUG=b/131205169 BRANCH=none TEST=buildall Change-Id: I7f581349713d30f10acb3797ab08b15aa2d50f00 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1584351 Commit-Ready: Daisuke Nojiri <dnojiri@chromium.org> Tested-by: Daisuke Nojiri <dnojiri@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: YH Lin <yueherngl@chromium.org>

Flapjack: Disable charging from BC 1.2 charger as USB-C charger Currently, if a charger shows Rp=USB on USB-C port, the charge manager chooses it and sets the max current to 500 mA even if it can provide higher power as a BC 1.2 charger. This patch introduces CONFIG_USBC_DISABLE_CHARGE_FROM_RP_DEF. When it's defined, a BC 1.2 charger won't be recognized as a USB-C charger. vpd: add a flag for optionally not creating VPD cache vpd_get_value checks if the vpd cache file exists. If the cache does not exist, it calls dump_vpd_log to fetch vendor data. Executing dump_vpd_log takes a non-negligible amount of time and is totally not necessary on a VM, since vendor data is unavailable in this case. This is causing a long running time on the cryptohomed pre-start script and related to test flakiness. Added a flag to vpd_get_value so that clients (cryptohomed) can opt to skip the vpd dump and cache creation. BUG=chromium:945489 TEST=PreCQ; test on a VM and chell device along with CL:1587815 BRANCH=None Change-Id: I093fbd3f706a404f490269e254603599a69838c4 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1585578 Commit-Ready: Wei-Cheng Xiao <garryxiao@chromium.org> Tested-by: Wei-Cheng Xiao <garryxiao@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Dan Erat <derat@chromium.org>

cryptohome: don't create VPD cache when calling vpd_get_value When cryptohomed starts on a VM, there is no VPD cache, since VM has no VPD. In this case, cryptohomed pre-start script spends a large amount of time (tens of seconds) on trying to get VPD values from flashrom, which always fails and is totally unnecessary. The long latency is causing test flakiness. Added the flag create_cache to allow cryptohomed to not fetch vendor data from flashrom. This should not affect real devices. If the cache doesn't exist when cryptohomed starts, there must have been some errors when the service in vpd-log.conf ran, and the flashrom error will likely to happen again in cryptohomed. BUG=chromium:945489 TEST=PreCQ; tested on a VM and chell along with CL:1585578 and made sure 1. this doesn't break a real device, 2. the crytohomed pre-start script runs for < 1 sec. Cq-Depend: chromium:1585578 Change-Id: I54bbdbbed234c0a8152ee2ad679f4a12df441e8c Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1587815 Commit-Ready: Wei-Cheng Xiao <garryxiao@chromium.org> Tested-by: Wei-Cheng Xiao <garryxiao@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Dan Erat <derat@chromium.org>
